title: The BADTIME! Collection
preview: The BADTIME! complete catalogue, recorded between 2021 and 2023.
summary: The _BADTIME!_ complete catalogue. This collection features the instrumentals and vocal tracks recorded between 2021 and 2023. This project was quickly abandoned when I realize that I am, in fact, the most _goated white boy absolutely dripped out in the sauce_, and that my voice doesn't suck, I was just getting the ropes of recording in a style that I liked.

tracks.title: GOOD WEATHER (HAPPY BIRTHDAY)
tracks.summary: This was originally a diss-track. It still kind of is. Now, I see it more as an electro-punk track, as its essence really gives 'sonically a shitpost'.

tracks.title: PICK THE FLOWER, PLANT SOME MORE, REPEAT
tracks.summary: Just something I threw together before work one day. Used a default VOX in FL Studio to create the vocal track, using a snip from a poem I wrote at the time. Or maybe a journal entry. I don't really remember.

tracks.title: IT'S FINE (Instrumental)
tracks.summary: The first track I ever made for this project. I think I was supposed to be studying for my major. I was not. In fact, I was smoking weed and fiddling around on my (then) brand new computer :)

tracks.title: IT'S FINE
tracks.summary: The vocal version of 'IT'S FINE'. Yeah.

tracks.title: mach 666 overdrive racecar fast mode - directors cut
tracks.summary: As I continue to write these descriptions I'm realizing that this entire project was named in a single night, in a manic frenzy. It's pretty funny though in retrospect.

tracks.title: whether or not i bought u flowers is trivial when looking at how much i loved u
tracks.summary:
A message to my ex. "You never bought me flowers", no, because you made such a fuss about how store-bought flowers were nothing compared to going out and picking a wild bouquet, oh the poetic gesture! How grandeur!
What a prissy bitch. I brought that upon myself, though, let's be honest. I miss her only sometimes, in moments I particularly hate myself.

tracks.title: my buddy once said this sounded like a grimes track but tbfh i disagree
tracks.summary: A bit self explanatory. If you're THAT dense, this song was compared by my buddy to Grimes, which I personally disagree with.

tracks.title: LIQUIFIED DDR4 RAM - 1996 CUT
tracks.summary: This was by far my favorite of the instrumentals. Music for driving fast asf boi.

tracks.title: KICK IT TO THE RIGHT SIDE
tracks.summary: This shit is BANGIN'!!! I have such a soft spot for this song. A breakup song, a revenge song, a spite song, it works for all of it. It was just fun to record my voice over my own beat (at the time) for once.

title: Take the Glory: The Series
preview: Would you be able to differentiate real vs. fake propaganda if it were shown to you side-by-side? The answer is likely not.
summary: Would you be able to differentiate real vs. fake propaganda if it were shown to you side-by-side? The answer is likely not. Take the Glory is a synthetically patriotic take on propaganda and its use in post-war society. Depicted is an androgynous face that's skewed by haze, flattened into a black and white rendering. Postured to be serious, sultry, and a careful amount of ambiguity, the viewer should be left wondering, have they secured their future and taken the glory while they had the opportunity? Different stylistic renderings are for different theoretical, real-world placements.

title: A Study of the Xerox machine: Physical Degradation
preview: Digital scrapbook artwork, printed, and scanned, and printed, and scanned, and printed, and...
summary: Digital scrapbook artwork, courtesy of the Internet Archive, BYTE magazine, and a littany of russian photography magazines. Printed, scanned, printed, scanned, you get the idea. Some of these were digitally altered even after the print/scan process. Years ago I turned these into woven blanket artwork and gave some away. Olivia, I want my "From one era into another" blanket back, lol.

images.alt: Lips with a text bubble "Basic"
images.summary: This was the first one of the project. I always liked this one.

images.alt: A man walking out the door with the text "Little Impact."
images.summary: I thought this one always looked like the representation of someone going towards the light...

images.alt: A dark image of a distorted face
images.summary: How I imagine GPT floating around the cybernetic void.

images.alt: Solve your personal energy crisis.
images.summary: Self explanatory. The graphic was ripped from an IBM ad, but I feel like in this context it gives the viewer a sense of dread. The energy crisis being due to technology draining the life from people.

images.alt: An orb in space with the text "Perfectly Balanced."
images.summary: This image was cool, the xerox totally fried whatever was on the edges of the paper. Or maybe that was the scanner. Either way...

images.alt: Scribbled handwritten text saying "Bend me towards the sun so that I can show you I can grow"
images.summary: This one was personal. The background was a photograph I took of a busted bus stop advertisement frame on Van Ness in San Francisco. The text was an iteration of a Jeff Buckley outtake that was never released. The idea is haunting, though. Asking the viewer to forcefully manipulate the position of the subject to force growth, as if the subject is begging for direction, relying with complete dependency. I ended up using this for the song 'bend towards the sun' by deo autem nihil as album artwork. The song is equally as haunting, in my opinion.

images.alt: CGI graphics over a checkerboard with the text "BREAKTHROUGH!" above
images.summary: This one struck me as a personal experience for graphic designers. As if, the subjects have been placed meticiulously after hours of deliberation, and the subject behind the canvas shouts in excitement.

images.alt: A shot of space, with the text "From One Era Into Another"
images.summary: I turned this one into a twin-sized blanket. Now she curses me to sleep on a twin-sized mattress. That joke will only make sense in its entirety to one person.

images.alt: Mountains with a dramatic sky
images.summary: This one took me forever. The mountains, foreground, and text effect in the background would not work together in the xerox-squared process. It was tough, but probably the most universally scenic of the series.

images.alt: A shot of a vacationing person with a Concord jet flying over
images.summary: RIP the Concord. Could've traveled across the world in a few hours, but SOME PEOPLE just had to complain about the noise. Grow up. Advancement comes with changes and waits for no one. And of course, only applies when I want something to change...

images.alt: A printer surrounded by printed text sheets, the most recent displaying a home logo
images.summary: I used this for the 'potentia per christange' release by deo autem nihil. It actually released some time around now four years ago. Time flies.

images.alt: Clean, Elegant, Powerful...
images.summary: This one always freaked me out. Looks and feels like a Benadryl nightmare.

images.alt: RUIN ME!
images.summary: By far my favorite of the series. I also turned this one into a woven blanket, and I ACTUALLY HAVE THIS ONE! HA! However, the message is ironic... I didn't realize how much I lived by this when I made it.
